item: The volume job, the single-file restore's log line, the import queue, the global error handler, the error journal and a failed background job's error line write what they catch with the passphrase taken out, through one set of helpers that take every secret in every shape, and every route that takes a typed key converts what escapes it, and the passphrase guard holds twelve modules and its own table of them

summary: The coordinator's check of #1318 (B1) named the volume job's own error handlers as the family of the engine's failure line, and its relay asked for the route layer's log lines too. VolumeBackupManager's runners caught Exception with the passphrase (and a restore's corpus passphrase) in scope and wrote the exception's words to the job's error (served by GET /api/backup/v2/volumes/status), the log and the run journal; restore_legacy_path logged its failure with _LOG.exception; and the import queue, which keeps the route's own response text in an item's error (served by the status route, persisted in import_queue.json), stored and logged what its handlers caught. Every such text is now scrubbed where it is made, through one set of helpers in src/monitoring/secret_scrub.py (scrubbed, traceback_text, log_failure) that take every secret the function holds, skip an empty one and withhold a text a later secret's marker would rebuild an earlier one in; the journal's cuts (2000, 8000, 500) come after the scrub; a log line leads with the exception's own line (the error journal cuts a record at 500 characters) and carries the scrubbed traceback as text and no exc_info. The route's responses are left as they are on the condition that no recorder keeps a response's text, which was read: errorlog.note_http_error keeps the status, the method and the path and takes no text (its unused detail parameter is gone, and a test pins the signature), the frontend reporter keeps uncaught UI errors only, and the queue scrubs where it records. The static walk (tests/test_p0_validation.py) holds eight modules, reads corpus_passphrase and the queue's self._passphrase as secrets, accepts status and partial only on a _PhaseError handler (the check's D3), and a coverage test holds its table to every module under src/ that holds the passphrase and writes what it catches, five left out each with its reason. D1 (the crash read's field count in OPEN_QUEUE) and D2 (which argument position a guard reads) of the check are fixed. Tests: 18 for the job, 8 for the route and the queue, the helpers' own and the walk's cases; 32 mutations of the helpers, the route, the queue, the request middleware and the guard and 21 of the job's own scrub sites are each caught. What stays outside is in OPEN_QUEUE.md: the responses and the global handler, runlog.run's journal, a path that is the passphrase, a form that is not the passphrase as typed, what a syntax walk cannot follow, and the columnar store's three records, which ride with the key-derivation change. The first merge of main added the lock screen to it: the findings PR (#1319) had put a handler in src/api/unlock.py that wrote a failed pool dispose with exc_info=True inside a function that holds body.passphrase, the coverage test found it, and it writes through log_failure now (a row of the table, a behaviour test that makes the dispose fail with the passphrase in its message). The coordinator's next relays (12:23, 12:32 and 12:33 UTC) widened it to the places every module's exception passes through: the global exception handler (src/api/main.py: the 500 response and its log record), the error journal the debug bundle carries (src/monitoring/errorlog.py, before its 500- and 1,500-character cuts) and a failed background job's error line (src/jobs/background.py, before its 300-character cut) take every passphrase the process holds (secret_scrub.held_passphrases(): the session's, OO_DB_PASSPHRASE and OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE) out of the exception's words and write the class where the writer names it, fixed words where it does not, and none of the exception's words when the scrub cannot run; a log_failure record carries the scrubbed traceback as an attribute so the journal keeps the frames. The scrub takes a secret out in every shape the code writes it in (as typed, as an SQL literal holds it, as repr and as JSON write it), all shapes of all secrets in one read, so a passphrase that contains another leaves no tail; the guard tells which secret a name is (a helper that takes one secret counts only in a function that holds one; a function that reads body.passphrase and body.corpus_passphrase must name both). 46 more mutations of the scrub core, the handler, the journal, the job's error line and the guard's lookup are each caught. Outside, in OPEN_QUEUE.md: uvicorn's own log of an exception after the handler has answered, a passphrase typed into the request being served, and the lone-surrogate UnicodeEncodeError (among its sites the unlock screen's compare in the already-open branch of unlock()). The one read of the head (14:16 UTC) found no trigger that exists today and the paths that would leak once one did, folded into the same push: every route that takes a key the process does not hold yet (unlock, create, encrypt, the encrypted backup, the single-file restore, the volume starts, the import queue's) is wrapped in scrub_and_reraise, which raises a RuntimeError that names the class and holds the scrubbed words, and the HTTPException details of those routes and of the two diagnostics starts are scrubbed where made; the read of what the process holds fails closed and takes no lock, and scrubbed always takes the held passphrases out; the shapes are a closure of two bases and four carriers three deep (at most 170), checked against the writers, with a floor of four characters under which the text that holds the secret is withheld; a failed job is scrubbed of the secrets it was started with and its record is written outside its handler; the journal's counts are read before the scrub; the browser sends its words whole and only the server cuts; the guard reads getattr, module aliases, ** splats, a bare re-raise, a new exception with no from None and a route's detail built from the exception; sixty-three more mutations are each caught. Outside, in OPEN_QUEUE.md: the core-limit entry (uvicorn's log, the sinks beside the journal, core dumps, the children's environment) and the derived key of the columnar store. The second fold (the coordinator's check of the first, F1 to F9) moves the release run's phases and their log line, the P0 check's exception text and problem lines, the restore child's error and result and the volume verify's decrypt reason onto the helpers that hold the passphrase (the per-needle helpers credit nothing in the guard now), withholds the text that holds a secret under the floor instead of leaving it in (an older store's correct short passphrase is held for the session), wraps the mailbox import's route and its background pull (the typed password), hands the unlock's checkpoint-close warning the typed key, empties the cache of shapes when the session's passphrase is cleared, holds OO_KEY_PASSPHRASE among the passphrases and takes note_http_error's unused detail parameter out; 47 mutations of the fold are each caught by a named test (two survived the first run and are tests now).
